messages:
irene_customer: Hey team — onboarding for Acero Labs (tenant: tl-acero-9). After completing the OIDC flow the console shows 'Provisioning complete' but there is no API key in the project's credentials tab. Can you check?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, irene. Can you paste the project ID and the urn/claim id you saw in the post-provision page? Also any screenshot helps.

irene_customer: Project: acero-prod-43. Claim shown on the final page: claim_7f3b2c. Screenshot: https://example.com/snap/claim_7f3b2c.png

alex_support: Thanks. I ran a quick lookup in the provisioning service and see claim_7f3b2c created, but it's bound to tenant tl-acero-9's parent org (org-temp-42) instead of the project. Possible race in the claim binding step. Paging @jordan_provisioner to confirm.

jordan_provisioner: Looking. Provision-bot logs show the claim was processed by the async binder but returned a 409 from the org service: "parent-org-locked". Binder retried but then a different worker bound the claim to org-temp-42. That matches what alex found. Repro steps I used: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://provisioner.internal/v1/claims/claim_7f3b2c` -> shows bound_to: org-temp-42.

alex_support: Can you explain why the claim would bind to the parent org? Is there a fallback when project binding fails?

jordan_provisioner: There is a fallback path in older binder versions: if project lookup fails with a transient error it attempts to bind to the org to avoid leaving claims unbound. We recently rolled binder v2.1.3 which should avoid that, but this tenant was routed to an older worker (AZ zone mismatch).

irene_customer: Oof. How do we get their API key into acero-prod-43 now? We need it for prod traffic tomorrow.

alex_support: Short-term: I can rebind the claim to the correct project manually. Long-term: we want to patch the routing so this tenant uses v2.1.3. Jordan, can you rebind and trigger key reprovision?

jordan_provisioner: I'll rebind now. Running internal command: `provisionctl rebind --claim claim_7f3b2c --target-project acero-prod-43 --actor jordan`

provision-bot: action_log: rebind started for claim_7f3b2c by jordan_provisioner

jordan_provisioner: Rebind completed. Triggering key generation: `provisionctl generate-key --project acero-prod-43 --claim claim_7f3b2c`

provision-bot: key_generation: success -> apiKey visible in secret store (ref: ssr://secrets/acero-prod-43/apikey)

alex_support: I pushed a small console refresh for irene's session. Irene, can you reload the credentials tab and see if the API key shows up?

irene_customer: Reloaded — key is visible now under "Service credentials". I tested a quick curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models` and it returned 200.

irene_customer: Big thanks. Any ETA on preventing this from happening to future tenants?

jordan_provisioner: Root cause: some binder workers in AZ-east still running v2.0.8 which has org-fallback. We'll force-deploy v2.1.3 to all zones and add a pre-check to block org-fallback behavior. ETA: 36 hours for rollout and monitoring.

alex_support: I'll update the provisioning incident tracker and notify SRE to watch for more rebinds. Marking this thread resolved for support. :thumbsup:

irene_customer: Great, thanks everyone! :heart:
